newsitem.title: AUSTRALIA: Air NZ sees wait on beyond rights.
newsitem.headline: Air NZ sees wait on beyond rights.

text.p: Air New Zealand Ltd said on Tuesday it would be a lengthly process before the Australain government makes any decision on the granting to Air NZ of rights to fly through Australia to other destinations.
"It's going to take a lot of work," Air NZ's government bilateral and regulatory affairs manager Irene King told Reuters after she gave a speech to an avaition conference here.
"It's a very difficult situation for us to be in," King said
AIR NZ has been lobbying for more Australian landing rights in order to better tap into lucrative Asian markets, a move against which Qantas Airways Ltd has been battling.
But King said it was difficult to put a definite time frame on the decision. Negotiations were also heavily dependent on how quickly a New Zealand government was formed, she said.
"(New Zealand First leader) Winston Peters is the key," she said, adding that some commentators were saying it might be six months before a New Zealand government was formed.
"When we get a government we would hope that the process would be speedy."
"We hope that the matter of further beyond rights will be settled soon because this is where the real benefit lies."
Under the new single aviation market agreement, Australian and New Zealand airlines were allowed to fly within and between both countries without restriction.
But there were still limits on beyond rights, preventing New Zealand airlines from taking passengers from Australia to a third country.
Air New Zealand bought a 50 percent stake in Ansett from TNT Ltd in September for about A$475 million.
